additivity_argument_B5.verdict: NOT ADDITIVE. Combined ceiling = max(latency, work) = latency side = 1.1032x (case9) / 1.1551x (case7).
reasons: 1 (MEASURED) Both attack the same quantity. iter25 already proved gap-1 (C-side interleave) and gap-3 (CV-over-GM elimination) attack THE SAME quantity - exposed cross-core waits - hence non-additive. This round measured directly that after eliminating 656/724 us of WORK, the increase lands exactly on cross-core exposed waits (case9 wait_id2 +38.01, wait_id4 +14.46, wait_id0 +10.84, wait_id5 +12.27 = +78.37 us). Work elimination opens NO new benefit channel; it merely converts pipe-busy time into the same batch of SEM waits => same source as the latency side => not additive.

2 (MEASURED) The work-elimination component is itself ~1.00x, so adding it changes nothing: case9 1.0060x, case7 1.0004x (p=0.669 ns). Even under an (incorrect) multiplicative combination, case9 would be 1.1032 x 1.0060 = 1.1099x, only 0.6% above 1.1032x - far inside measurement resolving power and attainment uncertainty. Its contribution to the combined ceiling is negligible.

3 (MEASURED) The absolute-upper-bound arm is NEGATIVE: W3 = all six segments gone = the absolute work-elimination bound reads +0.340% / +0.940% degradation (p=0.033 / p=0.00092, CIs entirely positive).
